text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

The panel composition tells you nothing useful here. You and the appointed candidate are both women, so sex-based preference between you is essentially impossible as an explanation. An all-women panel is also fairly common in policy and HR-adjacent ministry roles and isn't evidence of bias in itself. Raising it would read as grievance-hunting and would undermine your credibility on the point that actually matters.

What does matter: you have a legitimate, unanswered request for written reasons. Chase that in writing, cite the ministry's recruitment policy and any statutory deadline for feedback, and ask specifically how "leading international projects" was weighted and scored. If the scoring looks arbitrary or invented after the fact, that's your real argument.
